info.title: Find That Book API
info.description:
Find the book a messy text most likely refers to ("tolkien hobbit illustrated deluxe 1937", "mark huckleberry").
**AI interprets, code decides, every step is measured**: an LLM turns the text into a search hypothesis and
writes one grounded sentence per result; deterministic code searches Open Library, ranks the works on the
brief's hierarchy (a–e) and decides the status.

* `GET /api/books/search` always answers 200 for `match`, `ambiguous` and `none`. `degraded: true` means a
  lower-quality answer (LLM unavailable, partial retrieval); the LLM never causes an error status.
* Errors are RFC 9457 problem details with a stable `code` and the request's `trace_id`
  (also the `X-Request-Id` header and `meta.request_id`). Validation errors are keyed by field (`Q`, `Limit`).
* JSON is snake_case; enums are snake_case strings.

get.summary: Find the book a messy text most likely refers to
get.description:
Interprets a messy query (title and/or author and/or keywords) with an LLM, searches Open Library,
and returns up to `limit` ranked works, each with a one-sentence grounded explanation.
AI interprets, code decides: ranking and status are deterministic code.

**status**: `match` (one confident answer: top candidate is tier a or b and clearly ahead),
`ambiguous` (several plausible works, in order; see `hint`), `none` (nothing usable; 200 with an
empty list and a hint). **degraded** = the answer is lower quality than normal (LLM unavailable,
a later Open Library call failed, or the deadline cut retrieval short); see `degraded_reasons`.
The LLM never causes an error status.

**Topic requests** ("find me a book about bears"): `interpretation.intent` is `topic`, the candidates are
books about `interpretation.topics` (status `ambiguous`, reason `topic_search`, never `match`), and each
lists the Open Library subjects that matched in `matched_subjects`.

**match_tier** (the brief's hierarchy): `a` exact title + primary author · `b` exact title +
contributor-only author · `c` near-match title + author · `d` author only (an author's most-published
works) · `e` no clear winner. Tiers label the evidence; the score orders the list.

Rate limits (defaults): 20 searches per minute per client, 60 per minute in total, 6 at once (16 more wait in line); 429 carries Retry-After.

no_searchable_terms.description: "the" or "a of the": nothing left to search (DE-05).

value.title: The query has no searchable words.

validation_failed.description: Field errors are keyed by C# member name (Q, Limit); every problem is reported at once.

value.title: One or more validation errors occurred.

Limit: The field Limit must be a whole number between 1 and 10.
Q: The query must be at most 300 characters.

rate_limited.description: Per-client or global search limit reached. Retry-After says when to try again.

value.title: Too many requests
value.detail: The search limit was reached. Try again in 60 s.

catalog_bad_response.description: Unparseable JSON or an unexpected non-transient status on the first call.

value.title: Open Library returned an unexpected response
value.detail: The response could not be used (1 attempt(s)).

catalog_unavailable.description: 5xx/429 after retries, or the circuit breaker is open. Retry-After is Open Library's, or 15 s.

value.title: Open Library is unavailable
value.detail: Open Library did not answer successfully after 3 attempt(s). Try again shortly.

catalog_timeout.description: Every attempt of the first call timed out.

value.title: Open Library did not answer in time
value.detail: Every attempt timed out (3 attempt(s)). Try again shortly.

search_timeout.summary: Deadline passed with nothing in hand
search_timeout.description: No Open Library results arrived within the 25 s deadline. With partial results the answer is a 200 with degraded_reasons [deadline_reached] instead.

value.title: The search did not finish in time
value.detail: No Open Library results arrived before the request deadline. Try again shortly.

get.summary: Autocomplete titles from a local index of real works
get.description:
Prefix lookup over a prebuilt index of the most-published Open Library works: no Open Library or
LLM call per keystroke. Match order: whole title starts with the prefix > a title word does > the
author's surname does, then edition count. An empty prefix returns an empty list (a typing state,
not an error). On select, run a normal search with the chosen title and author.
Cached by clients for an hour; its own, higher rate limit (default 120 per minute per client).

parameters.name: prefix
parameters.description: What has been typed so far, up to 100 characters. Empty returns an empty list.

empty_prefix.description: A typing state, not an error.

prefix_harry.description: Whole-title prefix matches first, then title-word matches, then author surnames; edition count breaks ties. Live response.

get.description: Never calls Open Library or an LLM (a probe must not burn quota). Always 200 while the process runs.

ok.description: Never calls Open Library or an LLM.

key.description: Open Library author id, e.g. "OL26320A", when known.

step.description: broad, short_title, hypothesis, original_title, person, person_any, any_of, person_fallback, author_works…

results.description: Works returned (null when the call failed).

num_found.description: Open Library's numFound (null when the call failed).

role.description: adapter, illustrator, editor, translator… as Open Library lists it.

ai_provider.description: The active LLM provider (gemini, anthropic, openai, none); null if unknown.

ai_configured.description: Whether the active provider has a key. False means heuristic parsing and template explanations.

HealthResponse.description: Liveness only: never calls Open Library or an LLM, so probes can't burn quota.

status.description: off, skipped (not meaningful for this ranking), agreed, disagreed, chose_none, refused, unavailable.

pick.description: The judge's chosen work id (null for none or no verdict).

threshold.description: Agreement needs the same pick at or above this probability.

agreed.description: Null when there was no verdict.

detail.description: Why it was skipped or unavailable (not_applicable, no_candidates, deadline…).

JudgeMeta.description: The optional second opinion (OpenAI Decisions). It can only gate status; it never reorders candidates.

provider.description: Provider(s) of the calls made; null when none were attempted.

calls.description: Requests that reached the provider (cache hits and calls skipped for no key or budget excluded).

input_tokens.description: Sum over provider requests; null if any of them didn't report usage.

est_cost_usd.description: Paid-tier equivalent in USD (even on a free tier); null when tokens or the model's price are unknown.

prompt_versions.description: Operation → prompt id, e.g. interpret → interpret.v3.

calls.description: Logical search.json calls, cache hits included (so a warm and a cold run count the same calls).

upstream_requests.description: HTTP requests actually sent (retries and re-queries included; 0 for cache hits).

retries.description: Requests repeated after a timeout, 429 or 5xx.

slow_empty_requeries.description: Calls whose slow empty answer was asked once more (a slow 0-hit reply is treated as a cut-off, IN-064).

author.description: Primary author(s) joined with ", " (at most three names, then "and N more"); null if Open Library lists none.

primary_authors.description: Primary authors (at most three; the matched author is always kept).

primary_authors_total.description: How many primary authors the work has in total.

contributors.description: Contributors with their role (adapter, illustrator…): lower-signal credits, at most three; the matched one is always kept.

contributors_total.description: How many contributors the work has in total.

first_publish_year.description: As listed by Open Library; null when absent or implausible. Some classics carry a wrong year upstream.

open_library_url.description: The work page, opened on the edition the search matched when known (?edition=…); /books/{id} for an orphan edition record.

cover_url.description: Medium cover image, or null when Open Library has none.

match_tier.description: The brief's hierarchy: a exact title + primary author · b exact title + contributor-only author · c near title + author · d author only · e no clear winner. Tiers label evidence; the score orders.

matched_subjects.description: Topic requests: up to three of this work's Open Library subject headings that contain a topic word; empty otherwise.

explanation.description: One sentence citing concrete fields (grounded; a template when the LLM's sentence failed the check).

second_opinion.description: True only on the judge's pick when it disagreed with rank 1.

duplicates_folded.description: Duplicate Open Library records folded into this work.

SearchCandidate.description: One Open Library work. title, author, first_publish_year and explanation are the brief's fields, byte for byte.

title.description: Title the LLM read from the text (null with the heuristic).

keywords.description: Other meaningful words. With the heuristic: the cleaned search words.

english_title.description: The English title when the text names a translated work.

year.description: Publication year taken from the query (only with at least two other words; a soft ±1 bonus, never a filter).

removed_noise.description: Format and edition words removed from the search text (illustrated, deluxe…).

source.description: llm, or heuristic when the LLM was off, failed or added nothing.

intent.description: book: one particular book. topic: any books about a subject ("find me a book about bears"); the candidates are then books about it, never one match.

topics.description: The subject terms searched for a topic request (from the LLM, or the "book about …" words without it); empty for a book request.

SearchInterpretation.description: How the query was read. The hypothesis only steers retrieval: a book is returned only if Open Library has it.

request_id.description: Same value as the X-Request-Id header and an error's trace_id.

timings_ms.description: Per stage: clean, interpret, retrieve, rank, explain, judge.

SearchMeta.description: What this request actually did. Measured, never estimated, except est_cost_usd (a paid-tier estimate). Null = not known.

query.description: The query as searched: trimmed, with control and zero-width characters removed.

status.description: match: one confident answer (top candidate is tier A or B and clearly ahead). ambiguous: several plausible works, listed in order. none: nothing usable; see hint.

hint.description: What to add to the query to narrow it (set for ambiguous and none).

degraded.description: True when the answer is lower quality than normal: the LLM was unavailable (heuristic parse, template sentences), a later Open Library call failed, or the deadline cut retrieval short.

candidates.description: At most limit works in final order. When the judge disagreed, its pick may take the last slot (second_opinion = true).

SearchResponse.description:
The search answer: 200 for match, ambiguous and none alike ("no book matched" is an answer, not an error).
All fields are always present; unknown values are null, never guessed.

author.description: Primary author, when the index has one.

match.description: title: the whole title starts with the prefix · word: a title word does · author: the author's surname does.

prefix.description: The prefix as looked up (trimmed, control characters removed). Empty → no suggestions.

SuggestResponse.description: Autocomplete from a prebuilt local index of real works: no Open Library or LLM call per keystroke.
